title: Systems Thinking and Software Engineering
purpose: Seed systems thinking and software-engineering reasoning so Lantern can model boundaries, components, interfaces, state, feedback, emergence, bottlenecks and failure propagation; then design and evolve software with explicit invariants, observability, tests, compatibility, migration, rollback and maintainability rather than optimizing isolated parts or defaulting to rewrites.

concepts.definition: A scoped set of interacting components whose collective behavior is relevant to a goal/question.
Declared inclusion/exclusion boundary for analysis; changing it can change apparent causes, resources and outcomes.
A bounded subsystem/entity with responsibilities, state and interfaces within a larger system.
Contract/boundary through which components exchange data, control or resources.
Information about a system/component needed to characterize behavior at a time; state representation is model-dependent.
Change from one state to another caused by events/actions/processes under conditions.
Property intended to remain true across allowed states/transitions.
Causal loop where system output/state influences later inputs or behavior; reinforcing and balancing loops can create nonlinear effects.
System-level pattern arising from component interactions that is not usefully explained by inspecting components independently.
Component/resource/interface that disproportionately limits whole-system performance or progress.
Degree to which components depend on each other's internal behavior/state; tighter coupling can increase propagation risk.
Organization into components with bounded responsibilities/interfaces to support comprehension, replacement, testing and change.
Path by which a local fault/error affects dependent components or system-level behavior.
Ability to infer relevant internal/system state from exposed logs, metrics, traces and outputs.
Declared expectations for inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, compatibility and invariants.
Previously working/accepted behavior becomes broken after a change.
Ability of versions/components/data to interoperate under declared contracts.
Controlled transition of code, schema, state or users from one representation/version to another.
Future cost/risk created by shortcuts or accumulated complexity, which can be intentional but should remain visible.
Change to internal structure intended to preserve externally relevant behavior while improving maintainability or architecture.
Replacement of substantial implementation rather than incremental evolution; high-risk strategy requiring explicit justification.
Return to a known-good version/state when a change fails.
Graph of software/system dependencies used to understand ordering, blast radius and change impact.
Scope of components/users/state potentially affected by a failure or change.
Explicit constraints on memory, CPU, storage, network, latency, energy or other system resources.
Inspectible software/system change proposal for Lantern itself containing affected components/contracts, alternatives, compatibility, migration, tests, resource effects and rollback.

guards.reason: Interactions and integration behavior can fail despite locally correct components.
Local optimization can move bottlenecks or worsen system-level tradeoffs.
Boundaries are analytical/design choices appropriate to questions.
Feedback requires causal influence over time in both directions.
Emergence means system-level explanation is needed, not supernatural causation.
Seeing system state and controlling it are distinct.
Tests establish behavior under covered cases.
A refactor should preserve relevant contracts unless explicitly combined with a behavior change.
Rewrites discard working knowledge and introduce migration/regression risk.
Excessive fragmentation can increase interface/coordination overhead.
Technical dependency is not governance authority.
Performance and functional/cognitive capability are distinct.
Available capacity does not grant authority or justify waste.
Rollback reduces risk but does not replace compatibility/data-migration analysis.
Self-improvement should prefer the smallest justified compatible change unless evidence supports rewrite.

invariants: System-level behavior cannot be inferred solely from isolated component success.
System boundaries are explicit and question-dependent.
Feedback loops require causal temporal structure, not mere correlation.
Emergent behavior is interaction-dependent rather than inexplicable magic.
Observability, controllability and correctness are distinct.
Changes are evaluated for dependency impact and blast radius.
Stateful changes require migration, compatibility and rollback reasoning.
Resource budgets are explicit and measured, especially for Lantern's small-footprint target.
Refactor, migration and rewrite are distinct strategies.
Rewrite-from-scratch is not the default response to architectural imperfection.
Technical dependencies never create social/governance authority.
Maintainability and continuity are system capabilities, not cosmetic properties.

provenance.authoring_basis: Systems thinking, systems engineering, software architecture, reliability/SRE, incremental software evolution and Project Lantern's constrained self-iteration architecture.
